decisions.title: Returned outcome=failed on a nominal-coverage finding rather than a behavioral defect
decisions.rationale: The phase instructions are explicit: a gate that could not run is not a gate that passed, and nominal spec coverage must be reported as failed even when the underlying behavior looks correct on manual inspection. I traced cleanup-feature's Step 5.5 branch logic and validate-feature's zero-needs-user branch by hand and found no actual bug, but neither is proven by an executable test the way the sibling branches (absent-ledger in validate-feature, and all of Step 11.5) are -- scenario skill-workflow.11 is specifically the scenario whose entire content is a distinguishability property, which is exactly what a string-presence test cannot prove.

decisions.title: Did not attempt to fix the test gap myself
decisions.rationale: This phase's role is to produce evidence and a pass/fail verdict, not to implement fixes -- the orchestrator dispatches a fix agent on a failed outcome. I scoped the recommended fix precisely (two new executable tests, mirroring the existing pattern in test_no_ledger_path_survives_set_u / test_worktree_shaped_env_still_finds_the_ledger) so the next agent does not have to rediscover the gap.

next_steps: Dispatch a fix agent to add: (1) an executable test extracting cleanup-feature/SKILL.md Step 5.5's bash block and running it against three fixtures (no ledger, ledger with no needs-user entries, ledger with an open needs-user entry), asserting the three distinct outputs; (2) an executable test for validate-feature Step 11's CHOICES_COUNT -eq 0 path (ledger present, zero needs-user) proving the ✓ Choices: 0 needs-user row actually renders
Optionally tidy design.md's F8 wording to match the proposal.md fix from round-4 plan review (cosmetic, not blocking)
